_what: CONTENT DELTA — the regional review pass. 176 classes.
_cutFrom: the 173-class state as merged in PR #69.
_howToApply: Append the four arrays, then REPLACE every entry in `_modifiedClasses` by id.
_whyThisPassWasWorthRunning: The regional prompt was the one the design session predicted would be weakest — the handoff's rule is that outside models are strong on breadth and weak wherever the answer depends on what HouseSteady covers. **That prediction was wrong for this pass and right for the other two.** Its findings could not have come from general knowledge: hydrogen sulphide from the geology of the local limestone tablelands, and a food waste disposer being a septic load problem because the Ontario Building Code requires a substantially larger tank.
_theOnlyRealConvergenceInTheRound: Two classes were named independently by two reviews reaching them by different routes — **sulphur treatment** and the **outdoor wood boiler**. One arrived from a general water-treatment and rural-heating list, the other from local geology and local heating practice. **Agreement is only evidence where the reasoning differs**, and this is the only place in three reviews where it did.
_twoReviewsOneClass: `attic-fan` was reached by two reviews from opposite directions — one said attic and whole-house fans should split, the other that a whole-house fan is a warm-climate strategy that does not belong here. **Both resolve the same way**: this is a powered attic ventilator, whole-house fans are out of scope for this climate, and the label carried both and now carries one.
_oneFindingFiledInTheWrongPlaceOnPurpose: `no-snow-guards-on-steel-roof` is filed on `eavestrough` because **there is no roof class yet.** A sheet of ice releasing off a steel roof takes the eavestrough with it, so the consequence lands there even though the guard goes on the roof. **It moves when the building-fabric pass lands** — recorded rather than held, so the finding is not lost in the gap.
_scopeRulingThatClosedAFinding: The regional pass's largest structural finding was that **the frame assumes a property stays heated year-round**, which seasonal waterfront properties do not — full winterisation being a property-level event no object class can express. **The owner ruled on 2026-08-06 that seasonal and cottage properties are out of scope for the first years**, on the grounds that they are commonly built and patched below code. **So the assumption is correct rather than a gap, and nothing is owed.** Waterfront classes stay — year-round waterfront houses are a real segment and a dock comes out every autumn whichever way the house is occupied.
_notActedOn: Oil heating being over-weighted against propane — the gas classes already cover propane by fuel attribute, so no class changes. And a whole-home humidifier in drafty older stock causing condensation, which is real and is a judgement about the house rather than about the equipment — **that is assessment, and it is the line the frame does not cross.**

careCategories.label: Treatment solution refill
careCategories.note: Peroxide and chlorine injection systems. Consumable with a part identity — §1b. Regional: it exists here because the groundwater does.

careCategories.label: Boiler water treatment
careCategories.note: Outdoor wood boilers and hydronic loops. Untreated water eats a water jacket that costs more than the stove.

inspectionPoints.label: Evidence of pest intrusion
inspectionPoints.note: Mice nesting in a ventilator core, chewed wiring inside a generator enclosure, cluster flies in a window track. **Regional and constant in rural stock**, and it appears in no equipment manual — which is why an outside model that knows the region found it and two that did not, did not.

inspectionPoints.label: Backup heat present and configured
inspectionPoints.note: Air-source heat pumps at −25 °C. **The regional question is not whether a room is comfortable but whether there is a second heat source when the pump stops being able to extract any.**

inspectionPoints.label: Buried supply line and insulation
inspectionPoints.note: Outdoor boilers run insulated lines underground to the house. Heat loss there is invisible and it is most of the complaints.

opportunityConditions.label: Food waste disposer on a septic system
opportunityConditions.note: Regional and code-based: the Ontario Building Code requires a substantially larger tank to carry a grinder, so one fitted to an ordinary septic is a load problem rather than a convenience. **Neither of the other two reviews saw this.**

opportunityConditions.label: Air-source heat pump with no backup heat
Steel roof over an eavestrough with no snow guards
opportunityConditions.note: A sheet of ice releasing off a steel roof takes the eavestrough with it. **Filed on the eavestrough because there is no roof class yet** — it moves to the roof when the building-fabric pass lands, and it is recorded here rather than held so the finding is not lost in the gap.

classes.label: Sulphur and odour treatment
classes.note: Aeration or peroxide injection for hydrogen sulphide. **Named independently by two reviews from different directions** — one from a general water-treatment list, one from the geology of the local limestone tablelands. That is the only agreement in the review round that counts as two checks. It was previously falling into `water-treatment-other`, which is the bucket that exists to say a thing has no dependable maintenance — and this one does.

classes.label: Outdoor wood boiler
classes.note: **Named by two reviews independently.** A staple here for heating older houses and detached outbuildings, and it heats the house through buried lines rather than through a chimney in it — which is why nothing in the indoor solid-fuel classes covers it.

classes.label: Direct-vent propane space heater
classes.note: Regional. Heavily relied on for additions and seasonal rooms in older rural stock, and it is neither a fireplace nor a furnace. HouseSteady labour cannot touch gas, so its care carries `professional` throughout.

_modifiedClasses.label: Oil furnace
_modifiedClasses.note: Regional — real in rural Quinte, rarer in town. One care category apart from gas and it is the oil filter.

_modifiedClasses.label: Electric furnace
_modifiedClasses.note: No combustion, so four inspection points fall away including the heat exchanger. The same shape the fuel split takes in water heating.

_modifiedClasses.label: Air-source heat pump
_modifiedClasses.note: Regional, 2026-08-06: at −25 °C the question is not comfort but whether a second heat source exists when the pump can no longer extract heat.

_modifiedClasses.label: Heat recovery ventilator
_modifiedClasses.note: HRV and ERV merged — the care is filters, core cleaning and balancing either way.

_modifiedClasses.label: Attic fan
_modifiedClasses.note: CORRECTED 2026-08-06. Two reviews reached this class by different routes — one said attic and whole-house fans should split, the other that a whole-house fan is a warm-climate strategy that does not belong here at all. **Both resolve the same way: this is a powered attic ventilator, and whole-house fans are out of scope for this climate.** The label carried both and now carries one. Louvres seize long before anyone notices, because nobody looks in the season it is not used.

_modifiedClasses.label: Standby generator
_modifiedClasses.note: The exception in this system: a generator is an engine, and running and servicing an engine is not electrical work. Three care categories where the panel has none.

_modifiedClasses.label: Portable generator
_modifiedClasses.note: Splits from standby on stored fuel and on the interlock question. Fuel that sat two winters is why it does not start in the outage it was bought for.

_modifiedClasses.label: Garburator
_modifiedClasses.note: DUPLICATE RESOLVED 2026-08-06, and the correction leads per rule 14. This class and v0.2's `garburator` are one thing under two names — it arrived from outside review as `food-waste-disposer` and shipped before the tier-two pass reached v0.2's own id. **The id stays `food-waste-disposer` because it is already shipped and referenced; the label becomes `Garburator` because that is what a household in this region says.** Common, real, and everyone abuses it — and it sits on the boundary between appliances and plumbing, filed under appliances because it is one.

_modifiedClasses.label: Window
_modifiedClasses.note: Operating style is an attribute, not a class. Its count, storey and access are the per-object attributes the frame does not yet carry — the dimension the monthly service design needs for quotable work.

_modifiedClasses.label: Eavestrough
_modifiedClasses.note: The group-buy item — cleaning is seasonal and universal, and it is height work, which the owner ruled is HouseSteady labour.

_modifiedClasses.label: Outbuilding
_modifiedClasses.note: Stub component type at v1.11.0 — reported, not an error.
